Extract the result tables of a fitted model

Source: R/get-data.R
get_results.Rd

Returns one tidy table of a fitted model or related object, named by what, as a base data.frame; what = "all" returns every table the object offers as a named list. The tables available depend on the class of the object and are listed under Tables.

Usage

get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_covariates'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_transitions'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_enumeration'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'latents_comparison'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_bootstrap_lrt'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_start'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_diagnostics'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multilpa'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multilpa_covariates'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multilpa_transitions'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multilpa_enumeration'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multilpa_bootstrap_lrt'
get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model of this package, an enumeration grid, a model comparison, a bootstrap comparison, a starting-value set, a classification-diagnostics object, or the summary of any of them.

what

Name of the table to return, or "all" for every table the object offers. NULL (default) returns the primary table: the measurement model for a fit, the candidate grid for an enumeration, the test row for a bootstrap comparison and the entropy table for a diagnostics object. A name the object does not offer raises latents_bad_argument, listing the names it does offer.

...

Arguments for the requested table. Each table accepts only the arguments listed for it under Tables; any other argument raises latents_bad_argument.

Value

A base data.frame for a single what, whose columns are given under Tables, or a named list of such data frames for what = "all".

Details

Every object also has print(), which shows a compact overview, summary(), which collects its main tables (taking level and vcov_type where the model has standard errors), and as.data.frame(), which returns its primary table, the same as get_results(x).

Tables

Every fitted model offers these:

"profiles"

The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile and continuous indicator: profile, indicator, mean, variance, standard_deviation, mean_standard_error, variance_standard_error. Zero rows, with the same columns, when every indicator is categorical. Takes scale and data.

"responses"

The categorical measurement model, one row per profile, categorical indicator and category: profile, indicator, category, probability, threshold, probability_standard_error. threshold is qlogis(P(y <= category)) and is NA_real_ for each indicator's final category; a probability on its bound has an NA_real_ standard error. Zero rows, with the same columns, when no indicator is categorical. Takes data.

"covariances"

The within-profile residual covariance matrices, one row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators: profile, indicator, indicator_2, covariance. Under the diagonal parameterization the off-diagonal covariances are reported as exact zeros.

"ordinal", "count_means"

Fits with ordinal or count indicators only: the ordinal and count measurement models. Take data.

"counts"

Effective class sizes, one row per class at each level of the fit: level, class, effective_count (the summed posteriors) and effective_proportion. These differ from the modal counts in "classification" whenever entropy is below one.

"model"

One row describing the fit: its dimensions, likelihood, parameter counts, aic, bic_groups, bic_individual and its convergence and boundary diagnostics. The columns differ by family (a covariate fit adds its predictor counts); "information_criteria" has the same columns for every family.

"posteriors"

One row per individual and profile: row, group, profile, posterior, modal. Takes format.

"assignments"

One row per observation: the columns the fit was built from (or those of data), then profile, group_class where the model has one, uncertainty (one minus the posterior of the assigned profile) and one posterior_profile_* column per profile, plus posterior_noise for a fit with a noise component (whose cases are profile 0). Takes data and truth; with truth it returns a recovery table instead (see Recovery).

"classification"

Classification quality, one row per level and class: level, class, n_modal, proportion_modal, estimated_n, estimated_proportion, average_posterior, odds_correct_classification. Takes level. Under sampling weights estimated_n and estimated_proportion (and hence the odds of correct classification) are weighted posterior totals; the modal and average posterior columns describe the units supplied. The odds are Inf for a class classified perfectly (average posterior one to within rounding) and NA where they are undefined: a class with no modal members, or a single class, whose proportion is one.

"average_posteriors"

For the units modally assigned to each class, their mean posterior for every class: level, assigned_class, class, n_assigned, average_posterior. Rows sum to one within each assigned class. This conditions on the assigned class, whereas "classification_errors" conditions on the true class. Takes level.

"classification_errors"

The probability that a unit in one true class is assigned to another: level, true_class, assigned_class, probability, summing to one within each true_class. Takes level. On a membership-covariate fit this is a marginal summary over the fitted units, not conditional on the covariates. A fit with a noise component raises latents_unsupported_noise, as three_step() does, and "all" and summary() omit the table.

"bch_weights"

The BCH inverse-error weights, one row per unit and class: level, unit, assigned_class, class, weight. Takes level; a weighted regression should use one level, not "both". On a membership-covariate fit the weights invert the marginal error matrix and are not a conditional three-step correction. Not available for a fit with a noise component, as for "classification_errors".

"entropy"

One row per level: level, n_classes, n_units, entropy_sum, relative_entropy.

"residuals"

Bivariate residuals for every indicator pair, testing within-profile independence: profile, indicator_1, indicator_2, kind, observed, expected, residual, effective_n, statistic, df, p_value, p_adjusted. Takes data, by and adjust.

"information_criteria"

Every information criterion the package computes (see Information criteria). Takes format and definitions.

"sequences"

The assignments in occasion order, one row per observation: group, group_class, time, profile. Takes format. Raises latents_no_time for a fit made without time.

"sequence_summary"

One row per group class: group_class, groups, observations, mean_length, median_length, shortest, longest, complete, gaps. Raises latents_no_time for a fit made without time.

"starts"

One row per EM start: start, log_likelihood, converged, iterations, error and, where the family records it, boundary. Under search = "emEM", one row per start of the pool, with its kind, its stage ("final" when run to convergence, "screened" otherwise) and its screened_log_likelihood.

"data"

The data the model was fitted to, one row per observation in input order: the identifier (except for a single-level fit), the occasion where there is one, the sampling weights of a weighted fit (as rescaled for fitting) and the indicators under their original names. Columns the model did not use, including membership covariates, are not included; three_step() and r3step() therefore take data.

Fits with discrete group classes also offer:

"group_posteriors"

One row per observed group and group class: group, group_size, log_likelihood, group_class, posterior, modal. Takes format.

Tables specific to one family or object:

"gaussian_diagnostics"

Gaussian profile, membership-covariate, transition and cross-level fits that record these diagnostics. One row per Gaussian component and measurement context: context, profile, gaussian_mass, positive_rows, weight_effective_n, min_variance_ratio, min_standardized_eigenvalue, boundary. gaussian_mass sums posterior times normalized sampling weight over rows with at least one observed Gaussian indicator; positive_rows counts rows with positive contributions. weight_effective_n is the concentration measure (sum(a)^2 / sum(a^2)) for those contributions, not an identification guarantee; Gaussian mass is not this effective sample size. min_variance_ratio is the smallest component variance divided by its observed sampling-weighted marginal variance on the fitted scale, including between-component variation. min_standardized_eigenvalue is the smallest eigenvalue of the component covariance after standardizing every indicator by its observed sampling-weighted marginal standard deviation. Missing reference variation gives NA ratios. boundary concerns the absolute variance or eigenvalue floor. These descriptive measures use no automatic spike cutoff and do not alter start selection.

"profile_probabilities", "stages"

A multilpa fit. "profile_probabilities" has one row per group class and profile: group_class, profile, probability, group_class_probability. "stages" has one row per estimation stage: stage, group_classes, fixed, log_likelihood, parameters, parameters_with_measurement, converged. An ordinary fit has one "joint" row and a fit_staged() result has two; fixed is NA_character_ for a stage that estimated every block.

"coefficients"

A covariate fit. One row per estimated membership coefficient: level ("profile" or "group"), outcome, term, parameter (always "logit"), estimate. Standard errors are given by parameter_inference().

"transitions", "initial", "sequence_lengths"

A transition fit. "transitions" has one row per group class and ordered pair of profiles: group_class, from, to, probability, expected_count, stable, estimated, group_class_probability; it takes estimated and stable. "initial" has one row per group class and profile: group_class, profile, probability, prevalence, group_class_probability. "sequence_lengths" has one row per group: group, group_class, occasions, observations, complete.

"candidates", "best", "classification"

An enumeration grid. "candidates" has one row per candidate model: its name (candidate, first), its class counts, covariance model, log likelihood, parameter count, every criterion under both sample-size conventions, both entropies, the average posterior probability (AvePP) summaries of each level (avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, avepp_below and the same four prefixed group_) and the convergence, boundary, replication, warning and error diagnostics, including min_standardized_eigenvalue and min_gaussian_mass where Gaussian diagnostics are available. These are descriptive summaries, without an automatic cutoff or change to candidate selection. Failed candidates are kept with NA estimates and their error text. It takes cutoff (default 0.8): avepp_below and group_avepp_below count the classes whose AvePP is below it. A class with no modally assigned unit has no AvePP; it is excluded from the minimum, maximum and mean and counted as below the cutoff. A level with one class has NA summaries. "best" has one row per information criterion and sample-size convention: criterion, convention, candidate (the converged candidate with the lowest value), n_profiles, n_group_classes, model and value; what = "criteria" is accepted as a deprecated name for it. "classification" has one row per fitted candidate, level and class: candidate, n_profiles, n_group_classes, model, then the columns of a fit's "classification" table and that level's relative_entropy. Failed candidates and single-class levels contribute no rows.

"deltas", "knees"

Model-selection evidence of an enumeration grid, each taking using (default "bic_groups"). Neither selects a model. "deltas" has one row per candidate: candidate, its class counts and model, criterion, value, delta_profile (the decrease in the criterion from the converged candidate with one profile fewer, the same group classes and the same structure; positive means this candidate is lower), from_profile naming that candidate, and delta_group_class with from_group_class for one group class fewer. value and both deltas are NA for a candidate that did not converge, and a delta is NA when the smaller neighbour is missing or did not converge. "knees" has one row per line of the grid: direction ("profiles", along the profiles at fixed group classes; "group_classes", along the group classes at fixed profiles; "parameters", every candidate by its number of parameters, one line per structure), line, criterion, from, to, n_points, knee_candidate, distance, knee_without_largest (the knee when the last candidate of the line is left out), stable and note. The knee is the candidate furthest below the straight line from the first to the last candidate, measured perpendicular to it with both axes rescaled to 0-1. This is a simplified rule inspired by Kneedle (Satopaa et al., 2011), without its smoothing or sensitivity thresholds, so a very small positive distance can still name a knee. A line needs three candidates for a knee and four for knee_without_largest and stable; otherwise they are NA and note gives the reason.

"local_dependence"

For a fit with local_dependence: pair, kind ("categorical" or "continuous"), profile, item_1, category_1, item_2, category_2, probability, independent, ratio, covariance and correlation. A categorical pair has one row per profile and combination of the two items' categories: the fitted joint probability, the product of the two marginal probabilities (independent, the joint probability under independence within the profile) and their ratio; its covariance columns are NA. A continuous pair has one row per profile, with the pair's covariance and the correlation it implies; its category and probability columns are NA. A fit without pairs raises latents_no_local_dependence, and what = "all" leaves the table out.

"direct_effects"

For a fit with direct_effects, one row per effect: indicator, covariate, estimate (the change in the indicator's mean per unit of the covariate, the same in every profile), standard_error, statistic, p_value, conf_low and conf_high (Wald, from parameter_inference()). A fit without direct effects raises latents_no_direct_effects, and what = "all" leaves the table out.

"lmr"

The Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin (VLMR) and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin (aLMR) tests of an enumeration grid (Vuong 1989; Lo, Mendell and Rubin 2001; Vermunt 2024), one row per pair of converged candidates that differ by one profile (direction = "profiles") or one group class ("group_classes") at the same structure: direction, null_candidate, alternative_candidate, n_profiles, n_group_classes and model of the alternative, n_units (the independent units scored: groups, or observations without groups), parameters_added, lr (twice the log-likelihood difference), vlmr_p, adjusted_lr (lr / (1 + 1 / (parameters_added * log(n_units)))), almr_p, reference_mean and reference_sd of the weighted chi-square reference distribution, whose weights are the eigenvalues of Vuong's matrix of the two models' scores and Hessians, and note. The p-values are computed by Imhof's method to about 1e-9. A pair whose information matrix is singular, or whose candidate is on a boundary, keeps its row with NA statistics and the reason in note; warnings raised while scoring a candidate are recorded there too. Every candidate's information is computed, so the table is built only when asked for, and what = "all" leaves it out. A grid with no such pair raises latents_no_lmr.

"tree"

The flows of plot_tree(), on every grid, taking its arguments n_group_classes, n_profiles (n_classes on a regression grid), model, candidates, from, to and level (default "individuals"). One row per pair of classes in consecutive rows of each tree: tree (the tree's name, as in the plot list), level, from_candidate, from_class, from_share, to_candidate, to_class, to_share, mass (the share of all units the two classes share, the sum over units of the product of their posterior probabilities, weighted by sampling weights at the individual level), share_of_from and share_of_to (mass as a part of each class). Every pair is listed, including those that share no mass. Units are the rows and groups the fit counts (see drop_empty), weighted by their sampling weights at both levels. A grid with no tree raises latents_no_tree, a fit with a noise component latents_unsupported_noise, and what = "all" leaves the table out. The summary of a grid carries the default table only, without these arguments.

"comparison", "classification"

A compare_models() result. "comparison" is its table, one row per model. "classification", offered when every model is a profile, class, membership-covariate or transition model, has one row per model, level and class: model, then the columns of a fit's "classification" table and that level's relative_entropy; single-class levels are left out. The models themselves are returned by get_candidate().

"test", "replicates"

A bootstrap comparison. "test" is the one-row result; "replicates" has one row per simulated dataset.

"profiles", "responses", "profile_probabilities", "covariances"

A starting-value set: its Gaussian means and variances, response probabilities, profile probabilities and, one row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators, its covariances (profile, indicator, indicator_2, covariance).

"entropy", "classification", "average_posteriors", "residuals"

A diagnostics() object: the tables of the same names described above.

Tables of the other model families

Each family's first table is its default what; "all" returns a named list of every table (without "recovery", which needs data and truth). Tables with intervals take level, and vcov_type ("observed", "robust" or "opg"; NULL reuses the type stored with a regression fit). These objects also have coef(), vcov(type = ), confint(parm = , level = ), logLik() and nobs() methods.

Mixture regressions (mixture_regression())

"coefficients" (one row per class and term, with Wald statistics, p_adjusted by Benjamini-Hochberg over non-intercepts and exp_estimate for the binomial, Poisson and ordinal families; ordinal thresholds lead each class as terms "threshold:<lower>|<upper>"), "classes", "membership" (multinomial logits and odds ratios), "group_classes" (rows for two-level fits only), "fit" (bic penalised by the number of independent units, bic_rows by the number of rows, as flexmix reports it), "assignments", "groups", "fitted", "starts" (stage "screened" or "completed"), "classification" and "recovery" (by = "class" or "group_class").

Growth mixtures (mixture_regression(random = ))

The tables above plus "random" (random-effect variances, standard deviations and correlations, with intervals on the log and Fisher-z scales), "random_effects" (one row per person), "trajectories" (each class's mean trajectory with a band) and "individual" (each person's predicted curve); the last two take time. A multilevel growth mixture adds "group_classes" and "clusters", and its "fit" uses the number of clusters in bic (persons in bic_persons).

Additive fits (multilpa(family = "additive"))

"parameters" (class means, between- and within-group variances and class weights; variance intervals on the log scale, weights on the logit scale; adjust sets the p-value adjustment, "none" by default), "group_classes", "groups", "intercepts" and "conditional_intercepts" (each group's posterior intercept, overall or given each class), "assignments", "classification", "fit", "recovery" and "starts". effective_groups in "group_classes" is w^2 (1 - w) / Var(w), the number of perfectly classified groups that would estimate the class weight as precisely; below 50 the class's intervals carry a latents_weak_class warning.

Cross-level fits (multilpa(family = "full_cross_level") or "restricted_cross_level")

"profiles" (individual profiles, then the group classes' means of group means), "group_classes", "composition" (profile shares within each class: model-implied for the full family, a posterior-weighted description for the restricted one), "groups", "assignments", "fit" and "starts". The likelihood is a working likelihood, comparable only between cross-level fits of the same data.

General transition fits (lta() with transitions = "occasion", transition or initial covariates, measurement = "occasion", order = 2, mover_stayer = TRUE, weights, or ordinal/count indicators)

"transitions" (model-implied, averaged over the observed groups, with their sampling weights in a weighted fit; "initial" and "second_order_transitions" likewise), "transition_coefficients" (log odds of each move against staying, with odds ratios), "second_order_transitions" and "second_order_coefficients" (order = 2), "initial" and "initial_coefficients", "profiles", "responses" (categorical indicators: occasion, profile, indicator, category, probability), "ordinal" and "count_means" (ordinal and count indicators), "group_classes", "assignments", "fit" and "starts".

Pooled imputations (pool_imputations())

"estimates" (the pooled table), "imputations" (each imputation's aligned estimates) and "fits" (one row per imputation).

Transition and group-class family grids (enumerate_classes(time = ), enumerate_classes(family = ))

"candidates" (one row per candidate, its name first, with its likelihood, criteria, entropy and diagnostics) or "best", the row with the lowest criterion ("bic" by groups, the default, "aic" or "bic_individual"). "best" reports the lowest value of a criterion; it does not select a model. With one group class every family is the same model, so those rows share a likelihood. Candidates are extracted by name with get_candidate(); transition grids can also be passed to compare_models().

What "all" returns

A named list of every table the object offers, in catalogue order, each built with its default arguments; supplying any further argument raises latents_bad_argument. A table this object cannot produce (for example a sequence table for a fit made without time, or bivariate residuals for a family without discrete group classes) is omitted, so the names of the list show what was available. Only the conditions that mean the table does not exist for this object are skipped; any other error is raised.

Arguments the tables take

These are passed through ...; each table takes only those listed for it under Tables.

data

A data frame with one row per observation of the fit, in the order it was fitted in. NULL uses the columns the fit carries. The standard errors of "profiles" and "responses" come from parameter_inference() on these data. Without data, a fit that cannot supply them (bound-active, unconverged, singular information, a noise component) gives NA with a latents_no_standard_errors message; with data, the underlying condition is raised.

scale

For "profiles": "raw" (default) reports estimates in input units; "standardized" divides each indicator's deviation from its grand mean by that indicator's observed standard deviation, as plot(x, scale = "standardized") draws. The standard errors are divided by the same constant.

format

For the posterior tables and "sequences", "long" (default) gives one row per unit and class and "wide" one row per unit with one column per class. For "information_criteria", "wide" (default) gives one row and "long" one row per criterion and sample-size convention.

level

The classification level to report: "individuals", "groups" or "both". NULL (default) gives "both" for a fit with discrete group classes and "individuals" otherwise, as in diagnostics().

truth

For "assignments", one or more column names of data holding known labels to compare the assignments with. See Recovery.

by

For "residuals", "profile" (default) assesses each profile separately and "overall" pools them.

adjust

For "residuals", the multiplicity correction applied across the indicator pairs: "none" (default) or one of the stats::p.adjust() methods.

definitions

For "information_criteria" in long format, TRUE adds each criterion's formula and reference. Default FALSE.

estimated, stable

For "transitions", TRUE or FALSE restricts the table to the rows estimated (or not) from observed occupancy, or to the diagonal (or off-diagonal) cells. NULL (default) keeps every row.

Recovery

what = "assignments" with truth returns a cross-tabulation of the model's labels against known ones instead of the per-observation table: one row per class and truth value, with columns assignment (the model label compared against), class, truth (the column name), value, n and proportion (the share of units with that truth value assigned to that class). Several truth columns are stacked.

A truth column that is constant within every group is compared against group_class; one that varies within any group is compared against profile. The assignment column records which comparison was made. Group-level recovery counts each group once. Unused factor levels are omitted. For a fit without discrete group classes every column is compared against profile.

The model's labels are arbitrary, so mass off the diagonal indicates relabelling, not failure.

Information criteria

Let q be the number of free parameters, n the chosen sample size, and EN the classification entropy of the level matching that convention. The criteria are deviance = -2L, aic = -2L + 2q, bic = -2L + q log(n), sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24), caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1), awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n)), icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN, kic = -2L + 3(q + 1), and clc = -2L + 2 EN. clc, like icl and awe, uses the entropy sum; tidyLPA reports a CLC based on relative entropy, and the two values are not comparable.

Every criterion that depends on a sample size is reported under both multilevel conventions, "groups" and "individuals", using group-level posteriors under the first and individual-level posteriors under the second. Use one convention consistently across compared candidates. deviance, aic and kic carry convention = NA_character_. clc depends on no sample size, but its convention selects which level's classification entropy it penalises, so it is reported once per convention. Individual sample sizes exclude rows with no observed indicators, and group sample sizes exclude groups in which every row has none (n_informative_groups); the classification statistics of each level exclude the same rows and groups, as in Mplus. Where the group classification entropy is undefined, group-level awe, icl and clc are NA.

Classification quality

The odds of correct classification for class k is (p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r)), where p is the average posterior in the assigned class and r is the model-estimated class proportion. Values near one indicate classification no better than the class proportions alone; values of five or more are conventionally taken as adequate separation. It is NA_real_ when average_posterior is missing, or when it or estimated_proportion is zero or one, so a single-class solution always reports NA_real_. average_posterior is NA_real_ for a class with no modal members. n_modal and estimated_n differ whenever entropy is below one.

relative_entropy is 1 - EN / (n log K), between zero and one, higher meaning sharper classification; entropy_sum is the raw EN used by the entropy-penalised criteria, lower meaning sharper. relative_entropy is NA_real_ for a level with a single class.

A fit with individual profiles but no discrete group classes reports individuals only for level = "both" and raises latents_no_group_classes for level = "groups".

Bivariate residuals

"residuals" tests, pair by pair, the assumption that indicators are independent within a profile, weighting each observation by its posterior. data must be in the order the model was fitted in; the alignment is checked. A large residual indicates local dependence between two indicators, which otherwise tends to be absorbed by an extra profile. The p-values are approximate, and p_adjusted applies the correction named by adjust across the pairs. A fit with sampling weights uses them in the descriptive associations and effective_n; design-based inference is not implemented, so statistic, df, p_value and p_adjusted are NA for weighted fits.

References

Computing Science and Statistics, 29, 451–457. Cavanaugh, J. E. (1999). A large-sample model selection criterion based on Kullback's symmetric divergence. Statistics and Probability Letters, 42, 333–343. Biernacki, C., Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (2000). Assessing a mixture model for clustering with the integrated completed likelihood. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 22, 719–725. Bolck, A., Croon, M., & Hagenaars, J. (2004). Estimating latent structure models with categorical variables. See also

as.data.frame(), which returns the primary table alone, summary(), which prints every table, and diagnostics() for the classification tables gathered with a condensed reading.

Examples

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
get_results(fit)
#>    profile  indicator       mean  variance standard_deviation
#> 1        1     browse  0.5395774 0.5898715          0.7680309
